title: Kanya Sumangala Yojana 2026 - MKSY UP ₹25,000 Guide
meta_description: MKSY 2026: ₹25,000 in 6 stages birth to college. Income limit ₹3 lakh. Apply at mksy.up.gov.in. Helpline 1800-180-5145. Eligibility, docs, status.

hero.one_liner: Uttar Pradesh provides ₹25,000 to every girl child in 6 installments from birth to college enrollment - promoting girl education and fighting female foeticide

what_is_it: Mukhyamantri Kanya Sumangala Yojana (MKSY) is the UP government's flagship girl child welfare scheme launched in April 2019. It provides 25000 per girl distributed across 6 installments: birth (5000), vaccination at 1 year (2000), Class 1 admission (3000), Class 6 admission (3000), Class 9 admission (5000), and college enrollment (7000).

The scheme fights gender discrimination in UP rural areas: negative attitudes toward girls, female foeticide, early marriage, and prioritizing boys' education. By tying staggered cash transfers to educational milestones, MKSY makes girls economically valuable to families and incentivizes continued education rather than early marriage.

Eligibility is straightforward: girls born in UP to permanent UP residents, family annual income not exceeding 3 lakh, maximum 2 daughters per family (exception: twins in first delivery allow 3rd girl). Application is online at mksy.up.gov.in.
The portal allows real-time tracking of application status.

Impact has been substantial: Over 1 crore girls enrolled under MKSY as of March 2026. Field surveys show improved sex ratio at birth, increased girl school enrollment (particularly Class 6-9), delayed marriages, and increased college enrollments for girls.
Families now see daughters as assets generating government benefits.

extra_sections.title: Scheme Purpose
extra_sections.content: Kanya Sumangala gives ₹25,000 to every girl child in UP - distributed across 6 life stages from birth to graduation. Designed to reduce gender discrimination and encourage girl education in Uttar Pradesh.

Psychology of 6 Stages
content: Why not give 25000 at birth? Lump sums get diverted to non-education purposes (debt, repair).
Staggered installments ensure accountability. Stage 1 (birth) ensures girl registration and identity.
Stage 2 (vaccination) ensures healthcare. Stages 3-5 ensure education continuation.
Stage 6 incentivizes college - when dropout pressure peaks at 14-16, extra installments counter it.
The largest amounts (5000 at birth, 5000 for Class 9, 7000 for college) are strategically placed. Birth money aids infant mortality prevention.

Class 9 and college payments directly counter dropout when girls are most at risk of marriage. Field feedback: the 7000 college installment shifted mindset from 'marry her after Class 12' to 'let her finish college, get that 7000.'
Critical outcome: Families now see daughters as benefits generators, not liabilities. This psychological shift is the scheme's deepest impact, changing intergenerational attitudes.

Upload card. 2000 credited.

Upload school receipt. 3000 credited.

July 2041: College (BA degree) enrollment. 7000 credited.
Total: 25000 received over 22 years. Education fully supported at each stage.
Post-graduation, Priya employed; family's gender dynamics permanently transformed.

extra_sections.title: Eligibility Key Point
extra_sections.content:
Maximum 2 girl children per family. If twins are born, both are eligible.

Family income must be under ₹3 lakh/year. Only UP residents with Aadhaar-linked bank account qualify.

extra_sections.heading: Understanding the Six Installment Categories
content: Mukhyamantri Kanya Sumangala Yojana distributes its financial assistance across six specific stages of a girl child's life. Each installment is linked to a milestone, ensuring continued engagement with the girl's education and wellbeing from birth through graduation.
Category 1 provides Rs 2,000 at the time of the girl's birth. The family must apply within six months of birth with the birth certificate.
Category 2 gives Rs 1,000 when the girl completes all vaccinations within the first year. This links the scheme to the government's immunization program and incentivizes timely vaccination.
Category 3 provides Rs 2,000 when the girl takes admission in Class 1. Category 4 gives Rs 2,000 upon admission to Class 6.

These installments directly target the two stages where girl child dropout rates are historically highest in Uttar Pradesh - the transition from pre-school to primary school, and from primary to upper primary.

Category 5 provides Rs 3,000 when the girl takes admission in Class 9, addressing the secondary education dropout crisis. Category 6 is the largest installment at Rs 5,000, given when the girl enrolls in a degree or diploma program after completing Class 12.
The total benefit across all six categories is Rs 15,000 per girl child.

The staggered distribution design serves a dual purpose: it provides financial support at critical junctures where families might otherwise pull girls out of school, and it creates a monitoring mechanism that keeps the girl connected to the education system through periodic verification at each stage.

extra_sections.heading: Eligibility Criteria - Who Can Apply
content: The scheme is exclusively for families in Uttar Pradesh whose annual income from all sources does not exceed Rs 3 lakh. This income ceiling targets the economically weaker sections where the financial burden of raising a daughter is most likely to affect decisions about her education and welfare.
A maximum of two girls per family can receive the benefit. If a family has more than two daughters, only two can be enrolled under MKSY.

An exception is made for twin girls - if the second delivery results in twins and both are girls, all three daughters are eligible. Similarly, if a family has adopted a girl child, she can be enrolled provided the total count including biological daughters does not exceed two.
The girl child must be born in Uttar Pradesh and the family must be a permanent resident of the state. For Category 1, application must be made within six months of birth.

For subsequent categories, the application window is tied to the academic admission timeline. The family must have an Aadhaar-linked bank account in the state since all payments are made through Direct Benefit Transfer.

extra_sections.heading: Quick MKSY Eligibility Check
qualify: Daughter born on or after 1 April 2019

extra_sections.heading: Step-by-Step Application Process
content: The entire MKSY application process is online through the official portal mksy.up.gov.in. Here is the complete process from registration to receiving the first installment.
Visit mksy.up.gov.in and click on the Citizen Services Portal link. Register by providing your mobile number, name, and creating a password.
You will receive an OTP for verification. After successful registration, log in and click on Apply for Kanya Sumangala Yojana.

Fill in the application form with the girl child's details - name, date of birth, Aadhaar number (if available), and the category you are applying for. Enter the father or guardian's details including Aadhaar number, annual income, and bank account information.
Upload the required documents: birth certificate, income certificate, family photo, and Aadhaar cards.

After submission, the application goes to the Block Development Officer for verification. The BDO verifies the income certificate and family details and either approves or returns the application for correction.
Once approved at the block level, it moves to the District Probation Officer for final approval.

The approved amount is transferred directly to the mother's or guardian's bank account via DBT within 30 to 60 days of final approval. Track your application status by logging into the same portal and checking the Application Status section.
If the application is returned for correction, log in, make the necessary changes, and resubmit.

extra_sections.title: Documents Checklist for MKSY Application
extra_sections.content: Keep these documents ready before starting your application: Girl child's birth certificate issued by the local municipal body, family income certificate (annual income below Rs 3 lakh) issued by the competent authority, Aadhaar card of the girl child (if available - not mandatory for Category 1), Aadhaar card of the parent or guardian, bank passbook front page showing account number and IFSC code, family photograph, latest passport-size photograph of the girl child, and school admission proof for Categories 3 through 6.

extra_sections.heading: Documents Required for Each MKSY Stage
How to Apply for MKSY Online
MKSY ₹25,000 Breakdown - Exact Amount per Stage
content: The ₹25,000 total benefit is distributed across 6 milestones - not paid as lump sum.
Stage 1 (Birth): ₹5,000 within 6 months of birth.
Stage 2 (Vaccination): ₹2,000 after complete vaccinations.
Stage 3 (Class 1): ₹3,000 on admission to Class 1.
Stage 4 (Class 6): ₹3,000 on admission to Class 6.
Stage 5 (Class 9): ₹5,000 on admission to Class 9.
Stage 6 (College): ₹7,000 on enrolment to undergraduate degree.

extra_sections.heading: Common Problems and How to Solve Them
content: The most frequent complaint from applicants is delayed verification at the block level. BDO offices handle hundreds of MKSY applications and processing can take 2 to 4 months in some districts.

If your application has been pending for more than 60 days, visit the BDO office in person with a copy of your application acknowledgment and request a status update. You can also call the MKSY helpline at 1800-180-1111 for assistance.
Incorrect bank details cause payment failures in a significant number of cases. The bank account must be in the name of the mother or guardian - not in the girl child's name.
Ensure the IFSC code matches the specific branch, not just the bank. If payment fails, the portal will show a payment reversal status.

extra_sections.heading: Common Problems and How to Solve Them (continued)
content: Update the bank details on the portal and the payment will be reattempted in the next cycle.

Aadhaar seeding issues occur when the Aadhaar number linked to the bank account does not match the Aadhaar provided in the application. Visit your bank branch and verify that your Aadhaar is properly linked and seeded with your account.
This is a common requirement for all DBT schemes and resolving it at the bank end usually fixes the payment problem.

For Category 2 (vaccination completion), many families miss the window because they do not realize they need to separately apply for this installment after completing immunization. The Category 1 application does not automatically process Category 2.
You must log in again, select Category 2, upload the vaccination completion certificate from the nearest Anganwadi or Primary Health Centre, and submit a fresh application.

Impact of MKSY on Girl Child Education in UP
content: Since its launch in 2019, MKSY has enrolled over 10 lakh beneficiaries across Uttar Pradesh. The scheme has had measurable impact on girl child enrollment in schools, particularly in rural districts where the gender gap in education was most pronounced.

Districts like Bahraich, Shravasti, Balrampur, and Siddharthnagar - which historically had female literacy rates below 50% - have seen noticeable increases in Class 1 enrollment for girls since MKSY implementation began. While it is difficult to attribute all improvement to a single scheme, the financial incentive structure of MKSY combined with other state and central education programs has contributed to narrowing the gender education gap.

The scheme also serves as an indirect birth registration incentive since a birth certificate is mandatory for Category 1 application. In rural UP where many births historically went unregistered, the financial incentive of Rs 2,000 has motivated families to register births at the local municipal office, improving vital statistics data quality across the state.

extra_sections.heading: MKSY vs Similar Schemes in Other States
content: Several Indian states run similar girl child welfare schemes, and comparing them helps understand where MKSY stands. Madhya Pradesh's Ladli Laxmi Yojana provides Rs 1,18,000 in the form of National Savings Certificates purchased at different stages, with the full maturity amount available when the girl turns 21.
This is significantly more generous than MKSY's Rs 15,000 but has a longer lock-in period.

Maharashtra's Majhi Kanya Bhagyashree Yojana provides Rs 50,000 insurance cover and Rs 1 lakh at age 18 for families with one or two daughters. Rajasthan's Mukhyamantri Rajshri Yojana provides Rs 50,000 across six installments from birth to Class 12 completion - more than three times the MKSY amount.

While MKSY's total amount is lower than comparable schemes in other states, its strength lies in the installment structure that creates six touchpoints with the education system. This design encourages sustained engagement rather than a one-time benefit, and the online application process makes it more accessible than schemes that require multiple offline visits to government offices.

extra_sections.heading: MKSY vs Other State Girl Child Schemes

extra_sections.text: MKSY is not just about the Rs 15,000 - it is about creating six reasons for families to keep their daughters in school from birth through college graduation.

extra_sections.heading: Financial Planning Beyond MKSY - Maximizing Benefits for Your Daughter
content: While MKSY provides Rs 15,000 across six installments, smart parents can use this as a starting point to build a more comprehensive financial plan for their daughter's future. Combining MKSY with other government schemes and savings instruments creates a safety net that covers education costs from school through professional college.

Open a Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana account at any post office or bank immediately after your daughter's birth. SSY currently offers 8.2% interest - the highest among all government small savings schemes - and has a 21-year maturity period.
Depositing just Rs 250 per month from birth results in approximately Rs 1.9 lakh at maturity. Depositing Rs 1,000 per month yields around Rs 7.5 lakh.

extra_sections.heading: Financial Planning Beyond MKSY - Maximizing Benefits for Your Daughter (continued)
content: The MKSY installments received at each stage can be partially redirected into the SSY account to compound the growth.

Apply for the PM CARES for Children scholarship if applicable, and check if your district has any additional girl child schemes run by the District Magistrate's office. Many districts in UP have local schemes that provide additional financial support for girls who maintain good academic performance.
These are often poorly publicized and require visiting the Block Development Office to learn about them.

For families with slightly higher income, starting a mutual fund SIP of Rs 500 per month in the daughter's name through an equity mutual fund can create a corpus of Rs 8 to Rs 12 lakh over 18 years assuming historical market returns. This combined with SSY and MKSY can fully fund a professional degree at a state college without requiring any educational loan.

extra_sections.title: Pair MKSY with Sukanya Samriddhi
extra_sections.content: Open SSY right after MKSY Stage 1 birth payment. SSY offers 8.2% annual interest, tax-free under Section 80C.

extra_sections.heading: How to Check MKSY Beneficiary Status Online
content: If you applied for MKSY and want to check status, the portal allows online tracking.
Step 1: Visit mksy.up.gov.in, click 'Citizen Service Portal'.
Step 2: Enter username (mobile) and password.
Step 3: Go to 'Application Status' or 'My Applications'.
Step 4: Click any application to see status.
Step 5: For pending or rejected, click reference number to see issue and re-upload.

extra_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions About MKSY
content: Can I apply for MKSY if my daughter was born before 2019? No, MKSY covers only girls born on or after April 1, 2019.
Girls born before this date are not eligible regardless of the family's income level.

What if my family income crosses Rs 3 lakh after I have already enrolled? Once enrolled and approved, the benefit continues for all remaining categories even if your family income subsequently exceeds Rs 3 lakh.
The income verification is done only at the time of initial registration.

Can I apply for multiple categories at once if I missed earlier ones? Yes, if your daughter is already in Class 6 but you never applied for Categories 1 through 4, you can apply directly for Category 4.
However, you will only receive the installment for the category you are currently applying for - earlier missed categories cannot be claimed retroactively.

Is MKSY available for girl children adopted from other states? Yes, adopted girl children are eligible provided the adoption is legally documented and the adoptive family is a permanent resident of Uttar Pradesh with income below Rs 3 lakh.
The adoption deed must be submitted along with the application.
What happens if the girl drops out of school after receiving an installment? The scheme does not require repayment of already-received installments.
However, the girl will not be eligible for subsequent category installments since each requires proof of admission or enrollment at the corresponding educational level.

extra_sections.heading: How MKSY Connects With Other Central Government Schemes
content: MKSY works alongside several central government schemes to create a layered support system. The Beti Bachao Beti Padhao national campaign provides the awareness framework while MKSY delivers the financial incentive at the state level.
Families can simultaneously benefit from both without any conflict.

The PM Matru Vandana Yojana provides Rs 5,000 to pregnant women for the first living child and Rs 6,000 for the second child if it is a girl. If a family in UP receives PMMY benefits for the birth of a daughter and also enrolls her in MKSY Category 1, they effectively receive Rs 7,000 to Rs 8,000 for the birth event alone.
These schemes use different implementation channels - PMMY through the health department and MKSY through the women and child development department - so there is no duplication check between them.

For education-related benefits, the National Scholarship Portal offers pre-matric and post-matric scholarships for girls from minority communities and economically weaker sections. These scholarships can be availed alongside MKSY Categories 3 through 6 since they operate under different ministries.
Families should explore both state and central scholarship databases when their daughter reaches Class 9 to maximize the available financial support.

extra_sections.title: Helpline and Grievance Redressal
extra_sections.content:
For any issues with your MKSY application, call the toll-free helpline at 1800-180-1111 available during working hours. You can also email your complaint to mksy-up@gov.in with your application reference number.

For district-level issues, visit the District Probation Officer's office with a printout of your online application. If your grievance is not resolved within 30 days, file a complaint on the UP CM Helpline portal at jansunwai.up.nic.in - this escalates the matter to senior officials for faster resolution.

extra_sections.heading: Tracking Your MKSY Application Status Online
content: After submitting your application, track its progress through the MKSY portal at mksy.up.gov.in. Log in with your registered mobile number and password, then navigate to the Track Application Status section.

The status will show one of several stages: Submitted, Under Verification at Block Level, Forwarded to District Probation Officer, Approved, or Payment Processed. If the status shows Returned for Correction, log in and check the remarks field to see what changes the verifying officer has requested.

Make the corrections, re-upload documents if needed, and resubmit. The entire verification process typically takes 45 to 90 days from initial submission depending on the workload at your district office.

faqs.question: I have 3 daughters. How many get benefits?
faqs.answer:
Only 2. Maximum 2 per family.

Exception: If first delivery is twins (2 girls) then 3rd girl born, all 3 covered. Single births: only first 2 eligible.

Limit is strict.

faqs.question: Daughter born in Bihar. Can she get MKSY?
faqs.answer: No, must be born in UP. If daughter born outside UP, ineligible even if family now in UP.

faqs.question: Daughter born in 2018. Is she eligible?
faqs.answer: No, eligibility from 1 April 2019 onward only. No backdated benefits.

faqs.question: Portal says income exceeds 3 lakh but I earn exactly 3 lakh.
faqs.answer:
Limit is 3 lakh maximum. Get income certificate stating exactly 3,00,000 (no decimals).

Combined family income (both spouses) counts. If husband 2 lakh + wife 1.5 lakh = 3.5 lakh (ineligible).

faqs.question: Can I claim MKSY and Sukanya Samriddhi both?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Both independent schemes.

Suggestion: Deposit MKSY installments into daughter's Sukanya Samriddhi account for dual benefit - immediate cash support plus long-term compound growth at 8%+ interest.

faqs.question: Daughter not admitted to Class 6 due to migration. Can I claim benefit?
faqs.answer:
Technically no - scheme requires admission proof. But if administrative delay (late admission, transfer), get Gram Pradhan certificate stating girl engaged in studies.

Submit to District Probation Officer. Some DPOs lenient on administrative delays.

Try - worst case, lose that installment but other stages accessible.

faqs.question: Can I use claimed amount for wedding instead of education?
faqs.answer:
Money credited to your account - legally yours to use. But scheme intent is education.

Using Stage 3 money for wedding violates scheme philosophy. If milestones not met, future credibility questioned if audited.

Best: Use each installment for intended milestone.

faqs.question: What is the MKSY helpline number?
faqs.answer:
MKSY helpline is 1800-180-5145 toll-free. Department of Women and Child Development, UP.

Call Mon-Fri 10 AM to 5 PM.

faqs.question: What is the age limit for Kanya Sumangala Yojana?
faqs.answer: No single age limit - scheme spans birth to college. Each of 6 stages has its own age requirement: birth, age 1, age 6, age 11, age 14, age 18+.

faqs.question: How to check MKSY beneficiary status online?
faqs.answer: Visit mksy.up.gov.in and log in with registered mobile and password. Go to 'My Applications' to see status.

faqs.question: How much money will I get under Kanya Sumangala Yojana?
faqs.answer: Each eligible girl gets ₹25,000 across 6 stages. Raised from ₹15,000 effective FY 2024-25.

faqs.question: When was MKSY launched in UP?
faqs.answer: MKSY launched 25 October 2019 by CM Yogi Adityanath. Stage 1 eligible only for girls born on or after 1 April 2019.

faqs.question: Is there a last date for MKSY registration?
faqs.answer: No fixed annual deadline. Each stage has its own window: Stage 1 within 6 months of birth, Stages 3-6 in same academic year.
